item.title: Re: greg
item.content:encoded:
Was brought in by request, so here's my take on it.

The SCP itself seems rather disjointed to me I guess? It has these interesting abilities, only to uncontrollably teleport? Why does this happen, is there any reason to it or is it just used as a device to put it into humorous locations? Other than these initial details I don't really have much idea about the entity. Was it created in a lab, or always like this? How does it communicate to researchers and why? A few more details are needed to iron out just exactly what this SCP is.

The narrative part also has me a bit concerned, as there isn't much one. You have a initial containment, underestimating its abilities, then recontainent which I feel I've read several times before. This isn't exactly a bad thing however, you need to put your own unique spin on it. Then the whole makes friends with the doctor, only to have the doctor touch it seems a bit out of character for the Foundation. Usually something that emits a gas that elicits terror in humans would not be allowed to come into touch contact with a researcher. I'll echo a little of what cybersqyd said and ask where is the story leading? Is it building up to something after the doctor is killed, or does the article just end there?

All in all, the idea has potential but could use more refinement as listed above. Hope this helps, best of luck.

item.title: (Seking Greenlight) World of the Wars
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: In various small enclaves around the world, the belligerents of all the world's wars have small military contingents that never surrendered. In truth, these enclaves are actually entrances to an alternate universe that serves solely to keep wars going, and created these enclaves for that purpose. Here, not only do no real-world wars ever end, the various factions have their own political intrigues including new wars, espionage, and support for others.

Central Narrative: Begins with the Foundation's arrival in the holdout of the Obskurakorps, which they think is a more mundane holdout, or at least as mundane as the Obskurakorps can be. Talks end up going hot after the Obskurakorps takes them to be one of their predecessor organisations trying to infiltrate them, resulting in the death of the Obskurakorps' and Wehrmacht's Fuhrer and a war between them as to who will be his successor, and the unfolding use of this as a proxy war by various factions to try to get the side that would be most beneficial to them.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Seeing how societies change with anachronistic influences and eternal war, as well as how the balance of these wars shift and change in response to major events.

Additional Notes: This was largely inspired by post-WWII Japanese Holdouts, although the process of brainstorming it moved it far beyond being all that recognisable. I'm also not sure about having the Nazis be the ones who go into the Civil War, since I'm afraid that might be a bit overdone in alternate history scenarios where they win/don't get completely usurped.

item.title: The Ambivalent Monster
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Hook/Attention-Grabber: It's a standard fare weird alternate dimension. They send two D classes down there and spooky monster blah blah, until they realize the "monster" is a fairly reasonable sapient entity though distinctly not humanoid.

Elevator Pitch: It's an exploration of the Foundation's inhuman treatment of D-classes. The Eldritch entity that's down there is more concerned for the D-classes' well being than foundation personnel.

Central Narrative: Two D-classes are sent with cameras to document an extradimensional space (The Foundation at this point, knows it's unescapable, they're just curious). While wandering a mostly empty area, they stumble upon a friendly entity that appears concerned for them. The entity, while free to leave, stays to attempt to help the two get out, communicating back and forth and cooperating with the Foundation. Eventually, when the Entity finds a way to send them back with the help of the Foundation, they're rejected because it would be too costly, leaving the story ending at that.

Additional Notes: This would be a very character focused story. Though the story paints the Foundation in a bad light, I want to avoid the common tropes of the foundation being malicious idiots though, they have legitimate albeit incredibly cold reasons for their decision.

item.title: The designation creates the scp
item.content:encoded:
Has this idea been done yet?

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: Joke SCP

Genre (Optional): Comedy

Elevator Pitch: Any anomaly given the designation scp XXXX will undergo a drastic and irreversible personality change. Objects or entities designated scp XXXX will develop an immature, obscene personality, show significant decrease in logical reasoning skills, IQ and ability to make informed decisions and will take every possible opportunity to make obscene 'your mum' or 'thats what she said' jokes. This consciousness manifests in different ways e.g. afflicted computers will display text on a screen, buildings might manifest paint on walls as communication. It is not known how or why this designation produces such effects.

Central Narrative: When an entity with a consciousness was designated scp-XXXX, the researchers involved report a sudden change in personality and IQ in the entity. This was thought to be one of its anomalous properties, until it is discovered to be a manifestation of another scp, and is reclassified. Another anomalous object is given the same designation and this one develops a consciousness of an immature, obscene individual. After the foundation finds out and runs a series of tests with this designation, they designate the scp designation itself as scp-XXXX.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Jumping on the meta bandwagon- since the designation itself is an scp the designation itself has developed a conscious creating a paradox.

Additional Notes: May be able to use this scp to contain entities that are dangerous because of their superpowered mental faculties, possibly making this a Thaumiel scp.

item.title: Re: Philosopher's Blender
item.content:encoded:
Firstly, I would like to thank you for your quick response. I was expecting 1-2 days of waiting until someone review this.

I see, so there would be potential in this SCP idea, potential I was missing. That is…good to know. However, I wasn't just thinking about food, that was mostly just to show how normal people, in this case kitchen staff, would use it. In the long-term, I was thinking about Foundation personnel, for example, mixing together two different blood types to create a totally new blood type, with it's own pros and cons, pros being immunity to most blood-transmited diseases and cons being that the consumer is constantly thirstly unless drinking blood, human or otherwise.

However, stuff like electronics and incompatible things, that's something I was not really thinking about. Thank you for bringing this possibility to my attention. I will dwell on this idea.

As for the narrative side…truthfully, I don't really have an idea how this part should work. Yes, i did look up this forum for other ideas posted by others, however thinking that they might be new members and authors like me, I did not take their example for this part.

How should the central narrative look like? What specific…information should be in it? Like…

The blender is in actuality the experiment of a researcher with a Sc.D in science, who tried to make himself famous. In the end, using the help and resources of a mysterious contributor, he managed to create this blender which, well, mixes together ingredients/materials at an level not yet achieved in modern science. However, said researcher got absorbed, body and mind, into the blender, which now uses his knowledge of science and twisted mind to fine-tune the blending process and create all kinds of unique items. Limited conversation with the researcher can be made using the touchscreen.

That was at least the background for this SCP article. Is that a better example of an central narrative? If so, it's slightly hard to explain in this forum with the 400 words limit…

Nonetheless, I once again thank you for your review.

item.content:encoded:
SCP-5949 is a VHS tape appearing to be a film with the title Survival Of Halloween. The sticker appears to be scratched off and written over with a black marker. Placing SCP-5949 into a VHS player will send the victim using SCP-5949 into the film through anomalous means. Any recordable devices and people in the room will be taken into SCP-5949, any means of contact will be disconnected, Only after everything gets transported may personnel enter into the room. Once inside the victim will now be trapped and can’t exit the SCP-5949. After 10 minutes being stuck, entities (we will now refer to as SCP-5949-1) will attempt to attack the victim stuck inside mainly by beating the victim to death and then eating the corpse. The film will only end when everyone dies.

Deleted at -25 and three votes.

Rewrite by Quicksilvers pending.

SCP-5127 is a collection of multiple scorpion glass flowers (also known as “forget-me-not’s”) inside a tawny brown clay pot filled with sandy loam soil.

During visual exposure to SCP-5127, all brain cells in the exposed subject relating to memory will soften and loosen up in a way that will discard any memories that would have been created during visual exposure. This effect will continue around 5 (five) minutes after exposure, but will cease after. Should the subject still be in effect from SCP-5127 despite the passing of 10 (ten) minutes or longer, they are to be put into recovery and will no longer be eligible for testing, unless directed otherwise by the 05 council. Nausea during a state of recovery is common.

Deleted at -19 and three votes.

SCP-5458 is an anomalous Brunswick piano currently kept at Site-█. SCP-5458 must be constantly performed without any mistakes made when played. If any of this is violated, a transparent gas capable of corroding through human flesh will be released from the back of SCP-5458 within 20 seconds. The gas is classified as SCP-5458-1.

item.title: Re: Philosopher's Blender
item.content:encoded:
"Magic tool/appliance" and "weird thing that makes more weird things" are both heavily trodden territory on the site, but the concept here might still be viable.

I think you're missing the real potential here, though: A blender that makes super-healthy food isn't really interesting. A blender that blends any two things to produce a new thing resembling both, on the other hand, is very interesting- Blend small electronics. Blend abstract concepts. Blend things with incompatible properties.(say, a lit match and an ice cube) I'd suggest ditching the "decreasing returns" aspect- it doesn't add anything but another reason for the Foundation to put it in a box and ignore it.

On the narrative front- and I apologize for being a bit blunt here in the interest of clarity- what you have right now isn't really a narrative so much as a discovery log, and even within that "it just appeared out of nowhere and then was found by an agent by happenstance" is a site cliche you'll want to avoid. (Compare "It was a dark and stormy night…") It's up to you to figure out what sort of story you can tell using with this thing, but on the upside there's a ton of options. I'd suggest brainstorming in the direction of "mad logic"- What intersection of necessity and drunken wishing might spawn this thing? What would drive a mad scientist to usurp the laws of physics to construct it? What might someone with more curiosity than sense do with it? The answer only needs to make sense to the character; walking us through their chain of decisions in a clever way can be a great basis for a story.

Forum thread: Philosopher's Blender

item.title: Re: Freddy's Fishman (seeking Greenlight & Critique)
item.content:encoded:
Hey, I'm here upon request so lets take a look at what you got goin on.

Taking a look at the anomaly itself, it seems like it has the potential to be fairly interesting but isn't quite there. So far I see some sort of fish monster that was made, and it doesn't seem to go much further than that. Like said above, you give quite a bit on how it was found/came to but not real much on what happens with it afterwards. Infact, you kind of deflate the possibilities by limiting the SCP to be "rabid", which seems like a broad term and one you should avoid. Give some depth to the SCP, humanoid SCPs are usually interesting because they can communicate and express emotion. It seems this has the ability to do neither, and no opportunity to gain that ability. So for the SCP, I'd suggest to narrow it down to a more concise and focused object that allows for some depth and post containment development. I would also suggest rewriting the part of the SCP just being a kill monster, perhaps narrow down what triggers it instincts of flight/fight.

As for the story, I'll agree with cybersqyd on this one and say I'm rather confused on why the doctor needs to be so mysterious. You imply there are sinister things at work,but how do we know all this about the doctor, and how did he manage to infiltrate the Foundation? Is this GOI notable? Or is it the first appearance of them? You should also detail a bit of what you'd like to do with the story post containment. The whole infiltration plot seems like it can hold steam, but does the SCP actually have the ability to talk? And how are we finding out about the plot? Through an investigation? or perhaps a journal of the doctor left behind? I would examine these parts and narrow down the story some so that it flows better, and has a focus to it. Best of luck.

item.title: Youtube Channels Inspiration List (Work In Progress)
item.content:encoded:
There are a great number of Youtube channels that produce content that can be really useful and inspirational when you work on SCPs and tales. I've collected quite a few myself over the years, so I thought it would be useful to make a list of Youtube channels that can help us write.

What I really want is contributions. I'm going to start the list, but I want to expand it as much as possible. I'm going to use a format that will make it as fast as possible for people to find what they're looking for. If you contribute, please use the following format:

1. Include a link to the channel (preferably the channel main page, not just a video from the channel).
2. The name of the channel.
3. The category that they channel fits in (see categories below, might add more as time goes).
4. Description of the content on the channel. Try to include a little bit about who might be interested in the channel. See below for a framework.

Also note: The channel has to be somewhat directly relevant to writing SCPs. SCPs focus on phenomena that deviate from the norm. The list shouldn't include channels that delve into more mundane topics, even if those topics might be relevant to a story. It might be useful to research how a diesel engine works if you're writing a SCP focused on that topic, but it's not going to be even remotely useful to most people who write SCPs.

+ show block
– hide block

Youtube Channels

General Writing / Storytelling

Just Write
Link
Just Write focuses on looking at popular works of fiction, primarily movies, and trying to decipher what good lessons can be learnt from the work to improve your own writing.
Who is this for? Anyone who wants to use popular works of fiction as a foundation to improve their own writing.

Lessons from the Screenplay
Link
Lessons from the Screenplay, obviously, focuses on screenplays, often focusing each video on a single movie, going over the screenplay to explain what makes it so effective. Has a lot of videos that focus greatly on dialogue.
Who is this for? Anyone looking to cinema for tips on how to build tension and write beautiful dialogue.

SCP specific content

The Exploring Series
Link
To many on these forums, The Exploring Series was the gateway drug to the rest of the SCP community. Each video goes over a single SCP, telling the tale of the SCP in an interesting and captivating way, combining the story with images appropriate to it.
Who is this for? Everyone, but especially people who are yet not that familiar with the SCP foundation.

Real life - Investigation and policework

JCS - Criminal Psychology
Link
JSC focuses on the psychology of criminals, using interrogation videos as his primary source of information.
Who is this for? This channel is an invaluable asset if you want to create realistic interrogation scenes in your writing.

Real Life - Psychology

Dr. Todd Grande
Link
Dr. Todd Grande focuses on making psychological profiles of real-life murders and serial killers. Some of his profiles focus on other interesting people who are somehow outliers of society.
Who is this for? Anyone looking to create much more realistic and grounded characters, especially evil or malevolent characters.

Real Life - Philosophy

Academy of Ideas
Link
A channel that goes into great detail on some of the darker writers in philosophy and psychology. The channel explores archetypes, shadow projection, despair and similar topics.
Who is this for? Anyone who wants to learn more about the darker philosophers like Carl Jung, Nietzsche and Kirkegaard.

Real Life - Mysteries and peculiar phenomena

Lemmino
Link
Channel that focuses primarily on real life mysteries, like the Bermuda Triangle or Dyatlov Pass Incident.
Who is this for? Anyone looking to find information on the real life mysteries that often inspired SCPs.

Fiction - Horror

Acolytes of Horror
Link
Acolytes of Horror specializes in making fewer, but fairly long and in-depth analyses of horror. Primarily he analyses movies, but some of his videos focus on the historic influences on modern-day horror.
Who is this for? Anyone looking to really delve deep into the psychology and symbolism of effective horror.

The Vile Eye
Link
The Vile Eye makes psychological profiles of famous evil characters, from Nurse Ratchet in One Flew Over The Cuckoo's Nest, to Michael Meyers from Halloween.
Who is this for? Anyone who wants to create a memorable evil character.

Ryan Hollinger
Link
Ryan Hollinger makes videos where he analyzes various horror movies, discussing what makes them effective.
Who is this for? Anyone looking to widen their background knowledge on horror movies.

Fiction - Thriller and Drama

Fiction - Science Fiction

Isaac Arthur
Link
This channel focuses on hard sci-fi topics such as Dyson Spheres and Matrioshka Brains as well as hypothesizes about aliens. A lot of the material might be a bit too large in scale to fit into the SCP universe.
Who is this for? Anyone who's interested in hard sci-fi and civilizations on a galactic scale.

John Michael Godier
Link
The creator of this channel is a science-fiction writer who focuses on hard sci-fi, with an emphasis on realism. The content describes a lot of hypothetical science fiction phenomena.
Who is this for? Anyone who's interested in hard sci-fi, especially concepts such as multiple universes and alien civilizations.

Like Stories of Old
Link
This channel is very philosophical, it goes into deep detail on topics such as time travel, the hero's journey, global pandemics and empathy. It can help create an emotional and philosophical underpinning to any story you tell.
Who is this for? Anyone who wants to learn more about how sci-fi concepts and story tropes connect to a deeper philosophical and psychological truth.

Quinn's Ideas
Link
Quinn's Ideas focuses very heavily on the Dune universe, and as such goes into tremendous detail on topics such as psychic powers, genetics and omniscience. If you haven't read the Dune books, there are videos several hours long that go through each book. Has lately also started making videos on H.P. Lovecraft.
Who is this for? Anyone who wants to learn more about the Dune universe without reading all of the books. Also a great source of inspiration if you're writing on omniscience and related psychic powers.

Audiobooks

HorrorBabble
Link
Has all of the H.P. Lovecraft books, as well as many other horror writers such as Robert Bloch

item.title: Re: prix0rs the Cactus
item.content:encoded:
Hello! I am here per our IRC exchange to offer crit

Crit lives within
Yeeted and Deleeted

ConProcs

The temperature in its containment chamber is to be kept at a minimum of 28 degrees Celsius.

I would indicate which direction this errs. Is higher okay? Or is lower?

This is an otherwise very brief section so I have little to say. We just get right on into it and I'm good with that.

+++Description

Two arms extend from the central portion of its body.

Consider: "Two arms extend from center mass"

via levitation, usually at most 0.3 meters above the ground.

Language cleanup and significant digits. Consider: "levitation at an elevation of approximately 30cm"

SCP-XXXX is sentient and capable of speech via telepathy.

You might mean sapient. You might also want to say "communication via telepathy" rather than speech.

recording a corrupted version of its speech.

"corrupted version" is highly dubious.

It is capable of firing regular revolver ammunition

Since we just switched to the -1 I think it's probably fine, but, you could maybe stand to clarify the noun here a bit better in this passage.

bullets with a trajectory unaffected by wind,

Wind is only a factor at distances which are pretty well in excess of the range of a revolver.

It then traveled 6 kilometers across the city of Hollister,

I want to bring this up because the entire rest of this article is just one massive masquerade breach and you never cover or refer to that explicitly. There are "sightings" and nobody seems to call out the fact a levitating cactus is talking to them as it fights crime. If you want people to be nonplussed that is certainly an approach you can take, but we, as the Foundation, categorically should not be abiding this as "business as usual".

Video Logs

SCP-XXXX 'kicks' open the front door to a Starbucks.

This factually can't happen so I don't get why we're being coy. The door explodes inward, or, the door opens unassisted. This isn't very clinical even though I know exactly what you mean.

evaded capture for approximately 8 hours

This kind of begs the question of escalation. Why are we letting some random embedded agents chase this guy for a full day without sending help? Reduce the number, or send help.

technicians who smelled gunpowder in the water supply

I don't follow what this is implying and it never seems to come up again. You also probably wouldn't "smell" gunpowder; it only has a distinct smell when it's been fired/spent and that's not going to happen in water.

I liked the characterization of the video logs overall but I do have to warn you about your dialogue; you use a truly stupendous amount of exclamation points, and when they are so common they lose their meaning. Please strongly reconsider how you are applying this punctuation with an aim toward toning it down.

The best place to use an exclamation is after an interjection or command word. This is a way to suddenly or notably raise the level of emotion so you want to apply it rarely so people notice the departure from baseline. If every other line has an exclamation then that is a very excited and exhausting new baseline. I can clarify further if you want.

I would like to read this again to offer more thoughts as you explore the issues with the town, or alternatively, tighten up the timeline so those issues can be brushed away. As it stands, I am having trouble getting into what you're presenting because of the issues with the framework. I will say, in general, the central character does convey a good sense of identity but I think that their perseverance in the face of a less accommodating world might make them come through even more.
